title: Memory — Metaphysical Vignettes
content_html:
Memory — Metaphysical Vignettes

Retrocausality vs. Reconstruction

  • Thesis: Retrieval doesn’t expose a fixed past; it selects a past-consistent narrative under present constraints.
  • Process view: Moments “prehend” prior data into a new unity (process philosophy).
  • Quantum metaphor: Retrocausal models explore whether present measurements restrict allowable histories.
  • Practice: Treat recall as hypothesis testing under current goals and contexts.

Use in manuscript: Place beside Constructive Episodic Simulation to frame recall as selection among viable histories.
Sources: SEP—Process Philosophy; SEP—Retrocausality; Cramer 1986.

Context Drift and Retro‑Selection

  • Drift: Internal context slowly changes; retrieval reinstates a neighborhood of that context.
  • Inference: Present state biases which “version” of the past is reinstated.
  • Metaphysical link: Order in time arises because memory binds adjacent moments.

Use in manuscript: Insert where TCM/CMR is discussed to motivate metaphysical coherence of time via memory.
Sources: SEP—Process Philosophy; Bergson (duration) for philosophical resonance.

Present Constraints on Past‑Consistent Outcomes

  • Claim: Observation fixes outcomes consistent with boundary conditions; metaphor for how present aims curate recall.
  • Note: This is an interpretive metaphor, not a reduction.
  • Design cue: Encourage explicit question‑setting before divination/QRNG draws to shape interpretation.

Use in manuscript: Place near Quantum Randomness & I Ching
Sources: SEP—Retrocausality; Cramer 1986.

Plotinus ↔ Yogācāra (Storehouse and Return)

  • Plotinus: The One emanates Nous → Soul; recollection is return from multiplicity to unity.
  • Yogācāra: Ālayavijñāna as flowing substrate of seeds (bīja) that condition experience.
  • Bridge: Latent continuity becomes actual through attention and practice.

Use in manuscript: Add to Memory as a Void or Field as Collective Memory as a West–East concordance.
Sources: IEP—Plotinus; SEP—Yogācāra.

Remembering‑as‑Ecology

  • Ethic: To remember is to re‑member — to restore relations across scales (self, society, biosphere).
  • Practice: Stewardship = maintaining the archives of relation (biocultural memory).
  • Outcome: Coherent futures depend on how we curate collective memory today.

Use in manuscript:

Place within Memory × Nature (Select–Change–Reconstruct).
Sources: Stoic Logos (order), Wheeler’s “it from bit” as informational ecology metaphor.

Memory as Potential (Dunamis → Energeia)

  • Claim: Memory stores potential selections, actualized by present tasks.
  • Bergson: The past persists virtually; action summons what’s useful now.
  • Implication: Formal systems compress virtual pasts into stable operations.

Use in manuscript: Insert in Mind & Mathematics / Emergence
Sources: Bergson, SEP—Process Philosophy.

Memory as Self‑Organizing Logos

  • Stoic thread: Logos names an immanent rational order.
  • Informational thread: “It from bit” — reality constrained by information.
  • Bridge: Memory = the operational residue of order that guides new order.

Use in manuscript: Place alongside Mathematics as Illusion or Physics of Information
Sources: SEP—Stoicism; Wheeler “it from bit”.
